Coder in one, Writer in another, Researcher in a third. That&#x27;s all fine until you need to juggle a couple of different projects at the same time. It becomes hard to filter out signal from noise, and keep them in sync.</p><p>As a human and a team of humans, we tend to coordinate work in projects. Each project gets a spec, a plan, perhaps a Slack channel to communicate in. Then for each project, you&#x27;d have different tasks that someone takes on.</p><p>So I replicated that. Each project gets a Grok Bot channel and an entry in a Notion database. Note that this is an experimental pattern I&#x27;m still trying out.</p><div class="not-prose my-10 lg:my-12"><div class="border-primary/10 relative overflow-hidden rounded-2xl border"><div class="text-secondary mt-2 text-sm">One project, one channel, one roster.</p></div><h2 id="the-setup"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#the-setup">The setup</a></h2><p>I created two databases in Notion, Projects and Tasks. Then I created a <strong>projects</strong> (plural) Manager bot. This takes care of the higher-level coordination of projects and tasks. It has a Project Ops skill that takes care of creating a project, opening a channel, and staffing it with the right bots. It&#x27;s responsible for the meta work.</p><p>One project equals one channel in the sidebar, and the channel has the team of bots (and me) in it.</p><div class="not-prose my-6 grid items-start gap-6 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:my-8 [&amp;&gt;span]:my-0"><span class="not-prose my-6 flex flex-col items-start lg:my-8"><span class="border-primary/10 flex w-fit max-w-full justify-center rounded-xl border p-2 sm:p-3"><img alt="A project channel in the sidebar" class="rounded-md" loading="lazy" decoding="async" sizes="(min-width: 328px) 328px, 100vw" style="object-fit:contain;background-image:url(data:image/svg+xml;base64,);background-size:cover;background-repeat:no-repeat;max-width:328px;max-height:246px;aspect-ratio:1.3333333333333333;width:100%" srcSet="https://media.x.ai/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,onerror=redirect,width=328,height=246,f=auto/v1/website/grok-bot-guides-how-i-run-multiple-teams-of-grok-bots-02-channel-b9dc982a.png 328w,

https://media.x.ai/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,onerror=redirect,width=754,height=566,f=auto/v1/website/grok-bot-guides-how-i-run-multiple-teams-of-grok-bots-03-roster-b29d7a60.png 754w" src="https://media.x.ai/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,onerror=redirect,width=377,height=283,f=auto/v1/website/grok-bot-guides-how-i-run-multiple-teams-of-grok-bots-03-roster-b29d7a60.png"/></span><span class="text-secondary mt-2 block text-sm capitalize">The channel roster</span></span></div><p>Staffing rules I added:</p><ul>
<li>Reuse existing bots first. This can be a Coder, Researcher, Writer, or anything else that I&#x27;ve already defined.</li>
<li>Propose at most five bots besides the PM. Each channel is limited at six bots (just an arbitrary number I came up with).</li>
<li>Create a new bot only when nothing on the bench fits, and only after I say yes. This could be a specialist in a domain that gets reused in the future, or an ephemeral one only for this project.</li>
</ul><p>Here&#x27;s what the Projects database looks like:</p><span class="not-prose my-6 flex flex-col items-start lg:my-8"><span class="border-primary/10 flex w-fit max-w-full justify-center rounded-xl border p-2 sm:p-3"><img alt="Projects database in Notion" class="rounded-md" loading="lazy" decoding="async" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px, 100vw" style="object-fit:contain;background-image:url(data:image/svg+xml;base64,);background-size:cover;background-repeat:no-repeat;max-width:720px;max-height:540px;aspect-ratio:1.3333333333333333;width:100%" srcSet="https://media.x.ai/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,onerror=redirect,width=640,height=480,f=auto/v1/website/grok-bot-guides-how-i-run-multiple-teams-of-grok-bots-04-projects-efc1a6d9.jpg 640w,

Often the bots can accomplish a lot on their own, and I can just watch the cards getting moved around. Quite satisfying, to be honest.</p><span class="not-prose my-6 flex flex-col items-start lg:my-8"><span class="border-primary/10 flex w-fit max-w-full justify-center rounded-xl border p-2 sm:p-3"><img alt="Tasks moving across the board" class="rounded-md" loading="lazy" decoding="async" sizes="(min-width: 600px) 600px, 100vw" style="object-fit:contain;background-image:url(data:image/svg+xml;base64,);background-size:cover;background-repeat:no-repeat;max-width:600px;max-height:450px;aspect-ratio:1.3333333333333333;width:100%" srcSet="https://media.x.ai/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,onerror=redirect,width=600,height=450,f=auto/v1/website/grok-bot-guides-how-i-run-multiple-teams-of-grok-bots-05-tasks-f231942a.png 600w,

A board, a manager, specialists claiming tasks, a blocked column, a channel.</p><p>That is the experiment so far. If you run a team of bots, I want to see your setup. It becomes hard to filter out signal from noise, and keep them in sync.\"}],[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"As a human and a team of humans, we tend to coordinate work in projects. Each project gets a spec, a plan, perhaps a Slack channel to communicate in.
